methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $13M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Sarla Aviation is a Series A transportation company founded by Rakesh Gaonkar and Adrian Schmidt, having raised $13M to date. The relevant comp universe consists of 8 private frontier-transportation firms including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Pipedream, and FleetZero; no public comparables exist in this nascent segment.

A stage-progression methodology was the only applicable valuation anchor. Using total capital raised ($13M) as a proxy for Series A entry value and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage progression yields $26M. A peer-median approach was not viable: while three same-sector peers exist, none satisfy narrow-filter criteria (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier), and applying an all-sector median would introduce unwarranted noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $22M to $30M, with a median of $26M. This narrow band reflects reliance on a single method and underscores material uncertainty around stage-specific growth trajectories in an immature market. Key sensitivities include (1) execution risk inherent to frontier-tech hardware, (2) timing and terms of Series B fundraising, and (3) the applicability of standard step-up multiples to transportation subcategories with asymmetric capital requirements. Direct peer financial disclosure would materially reduce this range.
